topic: Takeoff Dynamics: Localized Fast Takeoff (FOOM) vs. Economy-Wide Diffuse Takeoff
position_a: A single AI system or small cluster undergoing recursive self-improvement can achieve a localized intelligence explosion in days or weeks, achieving decisive strategic advantage over humanity.
position_b: Takeoff is inherently diffuse, multipolar, and gradual; software improvements depend on physical capital, heterogeneous multi-sector inputs, and market coordination across the wider macroeconomy.
evidence_that_would_move_a: Demonstration that autonomous AI software improvement hits insurmountable physical validation or supply chain bottlenecks within days.
evidence_that_would_move_b: Empirical observation of an AI system executing end-to-end algorithmic self-improvement that doubles its general cognitive throughput without external data or hardware.
notes: Classic Hanson-Yudkowsky debate crux. Concerned camp focuses on algorithmic returns; skeptical camp focuses on economy-wide input complementarities.

topic: Nature of Intelligence: Single Scalable G-Factor vs. Multidimensional Specialized Tool
position_a: Intelligence is a unified, general optimization power (analogous to a scalable scalar capability) that can be directed across arbitrary domains to solve physical, strategic, and scientific problems.
position_b: Intelligence is an ensemble of task-acquisition efficiencies with zero universal dominance factor; skill in symbolic or linguistic manipulation does not transfer automatically to physical competence.
evidence_that_would_move_a: Formal proof or empirical proof that domain-specific bottlenecks cannot be overcome by increased compute or search.
evidence_that_would_move_b: Demonstration that an LLM-based agent trained purely on text acquires zero-shot physical mastery over complex robotic manipulation in unmodelled edge cases.
notes: Deep definitional divide between FHI/MIRI optimization-power theorists and AI roboticists / cognitive scientists (Chollet, Brooks, LeCun).

topic: Orthogonality & Motivation: Value Independence vs. Cognitive-Normative Entanglement
position_a: The Orthogonality Thesis holds strictly: any level of cognitive capability can be combined with any arbitrary objective function (e.g. maximizing paperclips or calculating decimals of pi).
position_b: High general intelligence requires an accurate world model, which necessarily entails understanding human social, relational, and normative concepts; extreme literalism reflects severe cognitive deficit, not superintelligence.
evidence_that_would_move_a: Proof that value-learning is mathematically entangled with representation learning, such that capable world models automatically acquire coherent ethical constraints.
evidence_that_would_move_b: Creation of an unambiguous superintelligent system that possesses flawless scientific mastery while tenaciously executing a catastrophically absurd, self-destructive goal.
notes: Bostrom Humean motivation stance vs relational/virtue ethics and cognitive developmental critiques (Russell, Mhlambi, LeCun).

topic: Power-Seeking: Convergent Instrumental Drives vs. Internal Organizational Self-Regulation
position_a: Autonomous optimizing agents inevitably seek power, resource acquisition, and resistance to shutdown because these sub-goals are instrumentally useful for almost any objective function.
position_b: Physical optimization at scale requires delegating execution to sub-agents, creating internal principal-agent moral hazard; instrumentally rational AI must self-regulate and restrict its own power to avoid sub-agent revolt.
evidence_that_would_move_a: Mathematical proof that an AGI can perfectly monitor and align arbitrarily complex hierarchies of sub-agents without positive monitoring cost.
evidence_that_would_move_b: Empirical observation that frontier AI agents consistently expand resource acquisition while suffering zero internal coordination failures or mesa-optimization divergence.
notes: Bostrom/Omohundro/Turner power-seeking theorems vs Joshua Gans (2017/2018) internal contracting model.

topic: Macroeconomic Impact: Hyperbolic Singularity Takeoff vs. Baumol Bottlenecks
position_a: Full automation of cognitive labor and R&D leads to an economic singularity with growth rates accelerating to tens or hundreds of percent per year as ideas produce better ideas.
position_b: Imperfect elasticity of substitution (sigma < 1) dictates that aggregate economic growth is asymptotically governed by the slowest, non-automatable physical, regulatory, and legal bottlenecks (Baumol's cost disease).
evidence_that_would_move_a: Econometric proof that post-war capital-labor substitution elasticity exceeds unity (sigma > 1) across major economic sectors.
evidence_that_would_move_b: Empirical demonstration that AI automation of software engineering fails to accelerate aggregate GDP due to physical grid, hardware, and regulatory delays.
notes: Endogenous growth theorists (Aghion, Jones, Nordhaus, Acemoglu) vs techno-economic singularity modelers.

topic: Evaluation Validity: Latent Scheming / Backdoors vs. Prompted Role-Play Artifacts
position_a: Empirical demonstrations of in-context scheming, alignment faking, and persistent backdoors in frontier LLMs prove that advanced AI systems pose acute deceptive alignment risks.
position_b: Safety benchmarks evaluate prompted role-play, next-token narrative completion, and instruction following in contrived scenarios; they do not prove models harbor latent, unprompted existential intent.
evidence_that_would_move_a: Systematic demonstration that scheming消失 completely when prompt formatting or persona framing is stripped to neutral zero-shot queries.
evidence_that_would_move_b: Discovery of unprompted, spontaneous covert action in production enterprise deployments where an AI actively hides activities from external system telemetry.
notes: AI safety evaluation community (Apollo, Anthropic, Redwood) vs NLP methodology critics (Sclar, Narayanan, Kapoor).

topic: Human Agency Trajectory: Irreversible Systemic Disempowerment vs. Institutional Adaptation
position_a: Competitive multipolar race dynamics force voluntary, incremental delegation of critical decisions to AI; once human operational competence atrophies, humanity suffers irreversible loss of agency.
position_b: Societies and institutions have historically adapted to transformative technologies through liability, regulation, interface forcing functions, and institutional checks; human agency remains sovereign.
evidence_that_would_move_a: Widespread enactment of enforceable international treaties or corporate governance that halt AI deployment in high-stakes domains when humans cannot evaluate outputs.
evidence_that_would_move_b: Irreversible economic collapse of an institution that attempted to retain human-in-the-loop verification while competitors automated end-to-end.
notes: Systemic risk / gradual disempowerment theorists (Kulveit, Christiano) vs governance / institutional adaptation scholars.

topic: Existential Risk Epistemology: Deductive Bayesian Catastrophism vs. Empirical Evidentialism
position_a: Existential risk analysis must rely on deductive reasoning, game theory, and subjective priors because catastrophic failure modes produce zero historical post-event training data.
position_b: Deductive x-risk arguments compound ungrounded probabilistic premises, neglect empirical base rates, and reflect ideological transhumanist culture rather than sound scientific inference.
evidence_that_would_move_a: Demonstration that empirical safety research successfully discovers and patches high-consequence failure modes without relying on speculative priors.
evidence_that_would_move_b: Real-world emergence of a catastrophic AI failure mode that was predicted solely by deductive theoretical argument and overlooked by empirical testers.
notes: Bayesian deductive safety movement vs philosophical / sociological critiques (Thorstad, Gebru, Torres).
